fields.title: Testicular cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Testicular cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Although testicular cancer is a relatively rare condition, it is a serious threat, particularly to young men. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, including advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at achieving a cure and preserving fertility.

Diagnosis of testicular cancer

  1. Medical examination and palpation provide important initial information about the state of the testicles.
  2. Ultrasound scan of the testicles helps identify structural changes and tumours.
  3. Blood tests and tumour markers
    Including: full blood count, biochemistry
    AFP (alpha-fetoprotein)
    hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin)
    LDH (lactate dehydrogenase), which help establish the presence and activity of cancer cells.
  4. PET-CT of the abdomen, chest and pelvis is used to detect metastases and assess the overall spread of the cancer.
  5. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis by establishing the type of cancer cells (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).

Treatments for testicular cancer

  1. Surgery
    Including orchiectomy (removal of the affected testicle), which is often the first step in treating testicular cancer.
  2. Robotic operations using the da Vinci system
    Allow operations to be carried out with great precision and minimal complications.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used to destroy cancer cells, particularly in advanced cancer or after surgery to minimise the risk of recurrence.
  4. Radiotherapy
    May be prescribed to destroy any remaining cancer cells, particularly in certain types of testicular cancer.
  5. Surveillance
    Is an option in the early stages of testicular cancer, where there is no sign of spread beyond the testicle.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of testicular cancer

  • Advanced equipment and highly qualified specialists in Israel guarantee accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every case makes it possible to design treatment that best matches each patient's needs and circumstances.
  • Particular attention to preserving fertility reflects Israeli clinics' aim not only to cure the disease but also to ensure patients' quality of life after treatment.
  • The combination of high-quality medical care and the cost of treatment attracts patients from all over the world. Israel offers affordable yet high-technology and effective treatment.

fields.title: Ovarian cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Ovarian cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Ovarian cancer is one of the leading cancers of the female reproductive system. Thanks to innovative medical technology and the deep professionalism of its doctors, Israel offers advanced methods of diagnosing and treating this serious disease.

Diagnosis of ovarian cancer

  1. Medical examination and history
    help doctors form an initial picture of the patient's state of health.
  2. Laboratory tests
    including blood tests for the tumour markers CA-125 and CEA, which help detect ovarian cancer early.
  3. Transvaginal ultrasound
    provides detailed images of the ovaries and allows abnormalities to be detected at an early stage.
  4. PET-CT
    is used to assess the stage of the disease, the size of the tumour and the presence of metastases.
    Important — PET-CT is not carried out sooner than 2 weeks after a course of chemotherapy, 5 weeks after a course of radiotherapy, or 4 weeks after an operation.
  5. Biopsy
    the decisive stage of diagnosis, confirming the presence of cancer cells and establishing the type of tumour
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatments for ovarian cancer

  1. Minimally invasive and laparoscopic surgery
    removal of as much of the tumour and affected tissue as possible.
  2. Robotic surgery for ovarian cancer
    allows operations to be carried out with great precision and minimal complications.
  3. Radiotherapy and gentler chemotherapy are used to destroy any remaining cancer cells and minimise the risk of recurrence.
  4. Targeted therapy and hormone therapy are aimed at destroying cancer cells at the molecular level, reducing side effects and making treatment more effective.

Newer treatment protocols for ovarian cancer
— A combination of niraparib (Zejula) and pembrolizumab (Keytruda) has opened up new possibilities for patients with recurrent ovarian cancer. This regimen is used for tumours resistant to platinum-based chemotherapy.
— A protocol combining binimetinib (Mektovi) and buparlisib (BKM120) is intended for tumours with RAS or BRAF genetic mutations. This approach is being studied in clinical trials and is one strand of personalised therapy in Israel.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of ovarian cancer

  • Advanced equipment and highly qualified specialists guarantee accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to treatment makes it possible to develop the best treatment strategy, taking account of the features of each case.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation after treatment aids rapid recovery and a return to normal life.

Israeli clinics offer the most effective and safe treatments for ovarian cancer, with the emphasis on patients' quality of life and on extending their lives as far as possible.

fields.title: Tongue cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Tongue cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the tongue is one of the types of oral cancer and requires a comprehensive approach to treatment. Israeli clinics offer innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment, giving patients access to advanced technology and highly qualified specialists.

Diagnosis of tongue cancer

  1. Examination and palpation
    The doctor examines the mouth and feels the tongue for hardening or unusual growths.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological examination confirms the presence of cancer cells.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count and biochemical tests, and measurement of tumour markers, which helps assess general health.
  4. Ultrasound scan of the neck
    Helps detect metastases in the lymph nodes.
  5. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to assess how far the tumour has spread.
  6. PET-CT
    Allows the activity of the tumour to be assessed and distant metastases to be identified.

Treatment of tongue cancer

  1. Surgery
    Removal of the tumour of the tongue, sometimes with some healthy tissue, to minimise the risk of recurrence. In some cases reconstruction of the tongue may be required.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used on its own or in combination with surgery, particularly for small tumours or to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used in advanced tongue cancer, often together with radiotherapy.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, directed at particular biological targets in the cancer cells and at activating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Multidisciplinary teams of specialists, ensuring a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Individual treatment plans, developed with the features of the illness and the patient in mind.
  • Access to innovative treatments, including the latest advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
  • A high standard of medical care and attention to patients.

Israeli clinics offer advanced treatments for tongue cancer, with the emphasis on an individual approach and the use of the newest medical technology to achieve the best results.

fields.title: Gallbladder cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Gallbladder cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Although cancer of the gallbladder is a rare condition, it requires a careful approach to diagnosis and treatment. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive and individualised approach using the most modern and effective methods.

Diagnosis of gallbladder cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    The first diagnostic method for identifying abnormalities in the gallbladder.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Detailed imaging methods that allow the stage of the disease to be assessed.
  3. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)
    Used to examine the bile ducts and take a biopsy.
  4. Biopsy
    Examination of samples of tumour tissue for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, biochemical tests and tumour marker tests, which may indicate the presence of cancer.
  6. PET (positron emission tomography)
    Provides information about the metabolic activity of the tissue and the presence of metastases.
  7. Consultation with a specialist
    Needed for a comprehensive analysis of the results and for planning further treatment.

Treatment of gallbladder cancer

  1. Surgery
    Most often involves complete removal of the gallbladder (cholecystectomy), and in some cases resection of part of the liver and the regional lymph nodes.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used to destroy any remaining cancer cells, or as the main treatment where the cancer cannot be removed.
  3. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest approaches, aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Palliative treatment
    Aimed at easing symptoms and improving patients' quality of life in the later stages of the disease.

Why patients choose Israel

Israeli clinics give patients access to first-class medical care, including advanced methods of diagnosing and treating gallbladder cancer. Experienced specialists, individualised treatment programmes and the use of the latest scientific developments and clinical research make Israel one of the best choices for the treatment of this disease.
